items.title: Howard Levy interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 11, 2025
items.q: I mean I’ve been listening to a bunch of Mingus lately. And I think that the guys who played with him...

ctx.x: Do you think the most challenging musical situations that you’ve been in over the years, have they mostly been self-imposed? By that I mean well you’re playing with Bela and wow this is tricky music. But my observation is that you invent your own challenges.

Yeah. I mean if you get with someone who’s like a kindred spirit, I mean Bela and I very much so, both playing very unstandard things on our instruments, you know, especially the harmonica and the banjo. The piano is another thing. And so I love a challenge as long as I can rise to the challenge. If the challenge is beyond me I say like let someone else play the gig. But if it’s something I feel I can really sink my teeth into it’s like man, yeah, let’s go for it, let’s do this tune that has all these really odd…

Can you think of a circumstance that happened to you, or you just mentioned that if you didn’t feel you could rise to a challenge you would suggest someone else do it. What kind of situation might that be?
